title: How much water to store
summary: At least 1 gallon per person per day for 3 days, 2 weeks if you can, in clean labeled containers.

sources.title: CDC: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply

blocks.text: Store **at least 1 gallon of water per person per day**. That covers drinking and basic sanitation. Plan for **3 days at minimum**, and for **2 weeks if you have room**.

blocks.text: Arithmetic: people x days x 1 gallon. Four people for 3 days is 12 gallons. Four people for 14 days is 56 gallons.
Unopened store-bought bottled water is the safest emergency source. Keep it sealed in its original container, in a cool, dark place. Use it before its expiration date.

items: Use food-grade water containers (FDA-approved, from camping or surplus stores). If you can't, use a durable, non-glass container with a tight lid and a narrow opening.
**Never** use a container that held bleach, pesticides or other toxic chemicals.
Wash the container with soap, then rinse it completely.
Mix **1 teaspoon of unscented household bleach** (5% to 9% sodium hypochlorite) into **1 quart (4 cups) of water**.
Put the lid on tight and shake so the solution touches every inside surface. Wait at least 30 seconds, then pour it out.
Let the container air-dry, fill it with clean water, and seal it.
Write **"drinking water"** and the **date** on every container.
Keep containers in a cool place, **between 50°F and 70°F**, out of direct sunlight, and away from gasoline and pesticides.
Replace water you filled yourself **every 6 months**.
When you pour, use a clean scoop or tap. Don't dip your hands or touch the inside of the container.

blocks.text: Keep one bottle of plain unscented household bleach (5% to 9%) with your water. See "Make water safe with bleach" for doses.
Don't ration drinking water unless officials tell you to. Drink what you need today and look for more for tomorrow. Soda, coffee and alcohol don't count: they dry you out.
